segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘Māra’.

segs.p: “Rūpe kho, rādha, sati māro vā assa māretā vā yo vā pana mīyati.
segs.e: “When there is form, Rādha, there would be Māra, or the murderer, or the murdered.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, rādha, rūpaṁ māroti passa, māretāti passa, mīyatīti passa, rogoti passa, gaṇḍoti passa, sallanti passa, aghanti passa, aghabhūtanti passa.
segs.e: So you should see form as Māra, the murderer, the murdered, the diseased, the boil, the dart, the gloom, the gloominess.

segs.p: Ye naṁ evaṁ passanti te sammā passanti.
segs.e: Those who see it like this see rightly.

segs.p: viññāṇe sati māro vā assa māretā vā yo vā pana mīyati.
segs.e: consciousness, there may be Māra, or the murderer, or the murdered.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, rādha, viññāṇaṁ māroti passa, māretāti passa, mīyatīti passa, rogoti passa, gaṇḍoti passa, sallanti passa, aghanti passa, aghabhūtanti passa.
segs.e: So you should see consciousness as Māra, the murderer, the murdered, the diseased, the boil, the dart, the gloom, the gloominess.

segs.p: Ye naṁ evaṁ passanti, te sammā passantī”ti.
segs.e: Those who see it like this see rightly.”
“But sir, what’s the purpose of seeing rightly?”
“Disillusionment is the purpose of seeing rightly.”
“But sir, what is the purpose of extinguishment?”

segs.p: “Accayāsi, rādha, pañhaṁ, nāsakkhi pañhassa pariyantaṁ gahetuṁ.
segs.e: “Your question goes too far, Rādha. You weren’t able to grasp the limit of questioning.

segs.p: Nibbānogadhañhi, rādha, brahmacariyaṁ vussati, nibbānaparāyanaṁ nibbānapariyosānan”ti.
segs.e: For extinguishment is the objective, destination, and culmination of the spiritual life.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called a ‘sentient being’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sattoti vuccatī”ti?
segs.e: How is a sentient being defined?”

segs.p: “Rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, tatra satto, tatra visatto, tasmā sattoti vuccati.
segs.e: “Rādha, when you cling, strongly cling, to desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form, then a being is spoken of.
When you cling, strongly cling, to desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

segs.p: viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, tatra satto, tatra visatto, tasmā sattoti vuccati.
segs.e: consciousness, then a being is spoken of.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, rādha, kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā paṁsvāgārakehi kīḷanti.
segs.e: Suppose some boys or girls were playing with sandcastles.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca tesu paṁsvāgārakesu avigatarāgā honti avigatacchandā avigatapemā avigatapipāsā avigatapariḷāhā avigatataṇhā, tāva tāni paṁsvāgārakāni allīyanti keḷāyanti dhanāyanti mamāyanti.
segs.e: As long as they’re not rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they cling to them, dally with them, treasure them, and treat them as their own.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, rādha, kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā tesu paṁsvāgārakesu vigatarāgā honti vigatacchandā vigatapemā vigatapipāsā vigatapariḷāhā vigatataṇhā, atha kho tāni paṁsvāgārakāni hatthehi ca pādehi ca vikiranti vidhamanti viddhaṁsenti vikīḷaniyaṁ karonti.
segs.e: But when they are rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they scatter, smash, and destroy them with their hands and feet, making them unplayable.

segs.p: Evameva kho, rādha, tumhepi rūpaṁ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha.
segs.e: In the same way, you should scatter, smash, and destroy form, making it unplayable. And you should practice for the ending of craving.

segs.p: Vedanaṁ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha.
segs.e: You should scatter, smash, and destroy feeling …

segs.p: saṅkhāre vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha.
Viññāṇaṁ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha.
segs.e: consciousness, making it unplayable. And you should practice for the ending of craving.
For the ending of craving is extinguishment.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘the cessation of the leash to existence’.

segs.p: Katamā nu kho, bhante, bhavanetti, katamo bhavanettinirodho”ti?
segs.e: What is the leash to existence? And what is the cessation of the leash to existence?”

segs.p: “Rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā—
segs.e: “Rādha, any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies—
this is called the leash to existence.
Their cessation is the cessation of the leash to existence.
Any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …
consciousness; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies—
this is called the leash to existence.
Their cessation is the cessation of the leash to existence.”

segs.p: Āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Pariññeyye ca, rādha, dhamme desessāmi pariññañca pariññātāviṁ puggalañca.
segs.e: “Rādha, I will teach you the things that should be completely understood, complete understanding, and the individual who has completely understood.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā rādho bhagavato paccassosi.

segs.e: “And what things should be completely understood?

segs.p: Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, pariññeyyo dhammo, vedanā pariññeyyo dhammo, saññā pariññeyyo dhammo, saṅkhārā pariññeyyo dhammo, viññāṇaṁ pariññeyyo dhammo.
segs.e: Form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
These are called the things that should be completely understood.

segs.p: Yo kho, rādha, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo—
segs.e: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.
And what is the individual who has completely understood?
It should be said: a perfected one,
the venerable of such name and such clan.
This is called the individual who has completely understood.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:
“Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.
The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti;
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

segs.p: na me te, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṁ vā brahmaññatthaṁ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.
segs.e: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti;
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

segs.p: te kho me, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.
segs.e: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:
“Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.
The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe…
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape … Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin …
There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand … Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:
“Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.
The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Yato kho, rādha, ariyasāvako imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti—
segs.e: When a noble disciple truly understands these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape,

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, rādha, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti.
segs.e: they’re called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:
“Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.
The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Yato kho, rādha, bhikkhu imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti—
segs.e: A mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, rādha, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto”ti.
segs.e: Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form.

segs.p: Evaṁ taṁ rūpaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Vedanāya yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: You should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

segs.p: Evaṁ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
saṅkhāresu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha.
Evaṁ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
Viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha.
Evaṁ taṁ viññāṇaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati …pe… anuppādadhamman”ti.
segs.e: Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Evaṁ taṁ rūpaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Vedanāya yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha.
segs.e: You should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

segs.p: Evaṁ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
saṅkhāresu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha.
Evaṁ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
Viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha.
segs.e: consciousness; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Evaṁ taṁ viññāṇaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhamman”ti.
segs.e: Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māro, vedanā māro, saññā māro, saṅkhārā māro, viññāṇaṁ māro.
segs.e: “Rādha, form is Māra, feeling is Māra, perception is Māra, choices are Māra, consciousness is Māra.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, rādha, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māradhammo, vedanā māradhammo, saññā māradhammo, saṅkhārā māradhammo, viññāṇaṁ māradhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form is of Māra nature. Feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of Māra nature.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, aniccaṁ, vedanā aniccā, saññā aniccā, saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are impermanent.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, aniccadhammo, vedanā aniccadhammo, saññā aniccadhammo, saṅkhārā aniccadhammo, viññāṇaṁ aniccadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of impermanent nature.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, dukkhaṁ, vedanā dukkhā, saññā dukkhā, saṅkhārā dukkhā, viññāṇaṁ dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are suffering.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
What is of a nature to suffer?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, dukkhadhammo, vedanā dukkhadhammo, saññā dukkhadhammo, saṅkhārā dukkhadhammo, viññāṇaṁ dukkhadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of a nature to suffer.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṁ anattā.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are not-self.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
What has a nature of not-self?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, anattadhammo, vedanā anattadhammo, saññā anattadhammo, saṅkhārā anattadhammo, viññāṇaṁ anattadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a nature of not-self.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to end’.
What has a liability to end?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, khayadhammo, vedanā khayadhammo, saññā khayadhammo, saṅkhārā khayadhammo, viññāṇaṁ khayadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to end.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to fall’.
What has a liability to fall?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, vayadhammo, vedanā vayadhammo, saññā vayadhammo, saṅkhārā vayadhammo, viññāṇaṁ vayadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to fall.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to originate’.
What has a liability to originate?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, samudayadhammo, vedanā samudayadhammo, saññā samudayadhammo, saṅkhārā samudayadhammo, viññāṇaṁ samudayadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to originate.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to cease’.
What has a liability to cease?”

segs.p: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo, vedanā nirodhadhammo, saññā nirodhadhammo, saṅkhārā nirodhadhammo, viññāṇaṁ nirodhadhammo.
segs.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to cease.
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.

segs.p: Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
segs.e: Form is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

segs.p: Vedanā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saññā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saṅkhārā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
viññāṇaṁ māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
segs.e: Consciousness is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

segs.p: yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.”

segs.e: “You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of Māra nature …”

segs.p: “Yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of a nature to cease.

segs.p: Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
segs.e: Form is of a nature to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

saññā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saṅkhārā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
viññāṇaṁ nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
segs.e: Consciousness is of a nature to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

segs.p: yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of a nature to cease.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.

segs.e: Form is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. …

segs.e: Consciousness is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

segs.e: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.”

segs.p: “Yo kho, rādha, māradhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo …pe….
segs.e: “You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is subject to Māra …”

segs.p: “Yo kho, rādha, samudayadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo …pe….
Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is liable to cease.
And what is liable to cease?

segs.p: Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
segs.e: Form is liable to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.

segs.p: Yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is liable to cease.”
The Linked Discourses with Rādha are complete.
